added_failure_derivation: From the reviewed run's own gate logs. The reviewed manifest declares no suite arms: baseline_suite and after_suite are both empty (classification.json manifest.data), and the reviewed change adds no product source or test, so there is no base/head pytest log to difference. The production derivation added_failures_from_gate_logs(None, None) returns unmeasured (count null, ids []), and the count is stored as unmeasured rather than as a measured zero.
artifacts: docs/figures/millisecond-converged-solve/cuda-graph-count/measure_cuda_graph_count.py: 432-line instrument; enabled arm 418 count observations, disabled arm 0; verdict executable_scoped_not_process_cumulative, growth 0, transient peak 2, after-drop 0, disabled max 0
evidence_inputs: Reviewed 8cbd46f3fdee9a61fbd48fb919cd7c0728d51567..37daba9a5d3f2594d182c27312967dd7556ae725 (five commits, 3087 insertions, git diff --check clean, reviewed worktree clean). The enabled raw log command_buffers_enabled.log shows the alive-graph counter oscillating 0..2 (instantiate->alive, destroy->remaining 0) throughout the ladder, so the count is transient rather than a stable retained count. The stored receipt.json summary came from --analyze-existing at revision a9c29fa7 and its after_cache_clear reading (release_events[0], :158) reverses the verdict the Titan job itself recorded (no_growth_observed, after-drop 2, released -1). The reviewed manifest's own baseline_suite and after_suite are empty.

findings.text: The post-release count is release_events[0]["count"], the FIRST destruction event between the before_drop and after_drop markers, not a settled re-read after the drop. In the recorded enabled log that window (command_buffers_enabled.log:3689-3852) holds the same per-execution instantiate/destroy churn seen throughout the ladder (:27->:36, :47->:56, ...), and the running `remaining alive executable graphs` reaches 0 many times between programs, and the after_drop marker itself read 2 (:3852->:3856). So the reported 'dropping 10 handles plus cache clear returned it to 0' (graphs_released_after_drop 1, receipt.json:2584) attributes to the drop a return to zero the measurement also exhibits without any drop; there is no drop-absent control. The landed verdict executable_scoped_not_process_cumulative therefore rests on a reading of the churn, not on a measured release.

The stored receipt labels itself revision 82f26d0a (:4, the Titan job revision) while its summary was produced by --analyze-existing at analysis_revision a9c29fa7 (:5); the two revisions disagree about the verdict -- the job's own receipt (titan-job-1280456.log:7) recorded {verdict: no_growth_observed, alive_executable_graphs_after_drop: 2, graphs_released_after_drop: -1} whereas the stored summary records executable_scoped_not_process_cumulative with after-drop 0 and released 1 (:2577, :2584) -- so a reader comparing the receipt to the locked revision 82f26d0a is reading a verdict that revision did not produce.

The report states 'Measurement revision: 82f26d0a' (:8) and then quotes the post-hoc re-analysis verdict block (:19 executable_scoped_not_process_cumulative, :25 graphs released at the drop boundary 1) as the measurement, without disclosing that the job at that revision itself returned no_growth_observed with released -1 (titan-job-1280456.log:7); the manifest's landing line carries the same unqualified claim, so the reversal is not visible to a reader of the record.

gate_arms_note: Read the reviewed run's own logs rather than re-running. The enabled arm emitted 418 count observations and the disabled arm 0 (receipt.json arms), so the disabled zero is a genuine control result. The first Titan job 1280453 failed the enabled arm's positive control guard (no count) and produced no verdict.

item_verdicts.done_when: The done-when names one Titan job with a disabled-command-buffer control arm and a drop-and-re-read step; the job ran (titan-job-1280456.log:7, enabled 418 count observations vs disabled 0, exit 0, Tesla P100), but its release clause is read from a post-hoc re-parse (analysis_revision a9c29fa7) that reverses the job's own receipt.
item_verdicts.goal: The goal is to measure whether the alive CUDA graph count accumulates per compiled executable or for the process; the enabled arm's twenty-program ladder (64x64..368x368) held the count at 1 at every completed-program marker with transient peak 2 (docs/figures/millisecond-converged-solve/cuda-graph-count/receipt.json summary), so it does not accumulate per distinct compiled executable.

justifications.evidence: The job ran with a real positive control (enabled 418 count observations vs disabled 0), but the stored receipt's summary was produced by --analyze-existing at analysis_revision a9c29fa7 (receipt.json:5) and records a verdict the job's own receipt contradicts (titan-job-1280456.log:7 no_growth_observed, after-drop 2, released -1).
justifications.fit: The figure obeys the data-ink rules (direct labels, despined, no grid) and the instrument guards are mechanism-worded, though the figure draws a flat-line-then-drop the raw churn does not cleanly show.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The ladder answers the posed alternative (growth_across_program_ladder 0 over twenty distinct programs, receipt.json), but the landing's release clause -- 'dropping 10 handles plus cache clear returned it to 0' -- is not measured independently of the per-execution churn the same log shows (command_buffers_enabled.log:27-36, 3689-3852).
justifications.scope_discipline: Every one of the five changed files is inside the out-of-repo declared paths (git diff --numstat 8cbd46f3..37daba9a5); receipt.json is 55 KB, below the 300 KB bound for a repository data file.
